{
  "segment_function": "Discusses the experiential difference between indoor and outdoor spaces, highlighting the interstitial and unenclosed nature of the outdoors, and connects this to Hannah Arendt's account of the embodied senses.",
  "claims": [
    {
      "claim": "The crucial difference between indoors and outdoors is that the indoors lends itself to comprehensive design as a whole to facilitate or discourage specific patterns, whereas outdoor spaces are not fully enclosed, making a totalizing form more challenging to impose.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "The crucial difference is simply that the indoors lends itself to being designed comprehensively , as some kind of whole, with an eye toward facilitating certain patterns of use, movement, and encounter and discouraging others; and while outdoor spaces have also been subject to the same sort of design, sometimes in a highly rationalizing and regimented spirit, the fact that they are not fully enclosed makes it more challenging to impose a totalizing\nform upon them.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "qualifications": [
        "outdoor spaces are also subject to design in a rationalizing and regimented spirit"
      ],
      "confidence": 1.0
    },
    {
      "claim": "Being outdoors as a sensate creature exposes one through the senses to a wider field of possibilities for the unanticipated or peripheral summoning of attention because the outdoors is intransigently interstitial.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "What matters about the outdoors, from this perspective, is that it is intransigently\ninterstitial; and to be outdoors, as a sensate creature, is to be exposed\nthrough the senses to a wider ﬁeld of possibilities for the unanticipated —\nwe might say , peripheral— summoning of one ’s attention.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "qualifications": [],
      "confidence": 1.0
    }
  ],
  "definitions": [],
  "distinctions": [],
  "examples": [],
  "objections": [],

  "references_to_other_sections": [],
  "unresolved_context": [],

    "The distinction regarding comprehensive indoor design versus the interstitial, unenclosed nature of the outdoors.",
    "Arendt's account of the embodied senses and their receptivity to the reality of life."
  ]
}
